title: Outsourcing and Third-Party Risk

maps.tested: Both readings rated Very Important; the handwritten sheet says to pay special attention to TPRM and outsourcing.
maps.specifics: Reported: 'outsourcing'. Core principle and standing exam trap: a firm may outsource the activity but never the accountability. Concentration risk in critical service providers, and the resilience implications, are the modern angle.

vardeezReading: ORR-12: Very Important (theme: TPRM, AML and outsourcing). ORR-13: Very Important (theme: TPRM, AML and outsourcing). ORR-5: untiered; use the crash course notes for ORR-1 to ORR-9, no Schweser needed. ORR-4: untiered; use the crash course notes for ORR-1 to ORR-9, no Schweser needed. selectors.name: Outsource the activity, never the accountability
selectors.what: A vendor or subcontractor fails and the question asks who remains accountable: the board and senior management of the firm, not the provider, the subcontractor or the supervisor; contracts, indemnities and subcontracting clauses allocate duties but never transfer accountability, and outsourcing trades operational risk for third-party risk rather than eliminating it (risk sharing, not risk transfer).

selectors.name: Concentration risk in a critical provider
selectors.what: Concentration risk when many activities depend on one critical service provider, or on few providers or few geographic locations (a firm-level risk, not only an industry-wide systemic one), and its resilience implications: single points of failure as resilience KRIs, low substitutability and high switching costs, back-ups and redundancy, impact tolerances and stress tests, contingency plans and an exit strategy.
